page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Left margin: seven quotation marks („) beside the lines from "ba.Neque" to "acumen fiant." Running head at top. Below the text: a centred summary line, then the chapter heading and the opening paragraph with drop cap.

p.i: pter diligenter oportet medicum contempla-ri actiones fingularum corporis partiu, quan-do imminuuntur, aut deficiunt, ratione indi-gentiæ nutrimenti, & quando acuminis mor-bi. Cunque primum contingit, cibus illico dandus est: si fecundum, maxime prohiben-dus. Qua in re sæpe labuntur nostræ ætatis medici, non discernentes alterutram actio-num noxæ causam. Quod antiquis medicis pri-or Hippocrates obiecit in libro secundo de ratione victus in morbis acutis in hæc ver-„ba.Neque sane horum ita peritos video medi-„cos, qui ut oportet dignoscât eas quæ in mor-„bis contingunt virium infirmitates, quæ ob„vaforum quam κυναγχὴν [?] Græci dicunt:et„quæ ob aliam quampiam irritationem, & quæ„ob πόνος, id est laborem, & quæ ob morbi„acumen fiant.
Victum docet qui sitienti infirmo cōuenit.
SITIS febricitantium quandoque taliest vehementia ut indicationem curationis suppe

page.notes: Drop cap "S" of "SITIS" is a large woodcut initial, transcribed joined to the word. The Greek word in the line "vaforum quam ..." is badly printed and uncertain; marked [?]. The catchword "suppe" is printed with a hyphen-like mark, read here without it. The centred line "Victum docet..." is a summary line, set as a paragraph. Left margin marks are quotation marks, not text.
